cause.proximate_text: The most likely cause of the event was the application of an ohmmeter across an open switch that had one side energized on the 250 VDC negative leg, which created a capacitive charge event. The stored charge in the long, partially energized control circuit rapidly equalized when contacted by the meter, producing a brief current pulse that momentarily energized the relay coil and generated a short isolation signal, resulting in unintended HPCI steam line isolation valve operations.
